item: streaming-speed (Android port, android-int-oct3 @ 90d32ca): make streamed Spotify→YouTube songs start faster on tap, skip and auto-advance, matching the iOS R12/R2/R3/R4/R5a/R7/R11/R8 intent
alreadyOnAndroid:
- R5a retries: already on Android. iOS copied them from here (CloudStreamProxy.kt:252-281: 401/403/404/410/429/5xx, MAX_UPSTREAM_ATTEMPTS = 4 at :93, refresh the same client first, 250 ms × attempt backoff). No change.
- Streaming instead of whole chunks, which is half of R2: the proxy reads googlevideo in 64 KB pieces (:360-366) and takes the size from Content-Range (:216-219). The pieces are never flushed to ExoPlayer, though (see currentBehaviour step 4), so in practice Android also waits for about 1 MiB.
- Pre-matching and resolving the NEXT Spotify song: already done for depth 1 only. MusicService.updateNextStreamPrefetch (MusicService.kt:1268-1299) waits 1.5 s, works only while playing, follows shuffle order (nextMediaItemIndex) and re-checks every 60 s. It matches and resolves the URL through the proxy (CloudStreamProxy.kt:83-87, :121-123; SpotifyStreamProxy.kt:116-127). Gaps:
  - no audio bytes;
  - no second song;
  - no Wi-Fi vs cellular rule and no Data Saver check;
  - the play gate reads the Spotify Connect wrapper, so it runs while Connect plays.
- Not blocking on remote config: nothing to port. Android has no remote client table: the clients are hard-coded in InnerTubeContexts.PLAYER_PROFILES (YouTubeStreamResolver.kt:207-226). The only remote properties reader (GitHubAnnouncementPropertiesService.kt:38-44) points at the upstream theovilardo/PixelPlay repo and has nothing to do with streaming.
- Skipping into a prepared next song: partly built in. ExoPlayer reuses the next item's loading period only in roughly the last maxBufferMs (60 s) of a song (DualPlayerEngine.kt:1017-1023). Crossfade's prepared playerB is thrown away on a manual skip (cancelNext on non-AUTO transitions, :527-529, :1384-1403).
- More aggressive than iOS today, and unbounded: every Spotify song played, plus its timeline neighbours (next and previous), is downloaded in full by the auto-cache, on any network (DualPlayerEngine.kt:533-555 → :1304 → AudioCacheManager.kt:132-137 → SongDownloadWorker.kt:93, :108).
- Overlapping clients: none. The chain is strictly sequential with 15 s per client (YouTubeStreamResolver.kt:262-264).
- Parallel ('fan-out') matching: none. TrackMatcher.findMatch runs its searches one after another (TrackMatcher.kt:56-64).
- Timing diagnostics: only the aggregate PLAYBACK_PREPARE (buffering → ready, DualPlayerEngine.kt:601-615). There is no per-step breakdown and no stream-start view.
currentBehaviour:
Read-only trace of /home/user/android-wt/base (android-int-oct3, 90d32ca). Nothing was measured on a device. Library facts were checked in the Gradle cache with javap: Media3 1.10.1, Ktor 3.5.0 (gradle/libs.versions.toml:32, :48).

TAP → FIRST AUDIO (Spotify track, no local copy). Every step below runs one after the other:
1. The UI awaits PlaybackDispatchStateHolder.buildResolvedPlaybackMediaItem (PlaybackDispatchStateHolder.kt:898-903), which calls DualPlayerEngine.resolveCloudUri (DualPlayerEngine.kt:1281-1317).
   - Its comment says it pre-resolves YouTube. It does not. It only:
     - checks the offline/auto cache with getPlayableFile (a Room read under AudioCacheManager's mutationLock, AudioCacheManager.kt:122-130);
     - calls maybeAutoCache (:1304);
     - starts the Ktor proxy lazily on the first Spotify song of the process (ensureReady :1308; CloudStreamProxy.kt:100-114);
     - builds the 127.0.0.1 URL.
   - maybeAutoCache enqueues a SongDownloadWorker for the WHOLE song with NetworkType.CONNECTED, which includes cellular and Data Saver (SongDownloadWorker.kt:93, :108). That job downloads the same song through the same proxy (AudioCacheManager.kt:201-216), so it can compete with the player's first bytes.
2. On ExoPlayer's loader thread, the ResolvingDataSource resolver runs resolveCloudUri again with runBlocking and a 25 s cap (DualPlayerEngine.kt:1098-1132). DefaultHttpDataSource (30 s timeouts, :1143-1147) then opens the proxy with no Range header.
3. In the proxy (CloudStreamProxy.kt:224-391), getOrFetchStreamUrl has a 25 s cap (:209-210) and a per-id shared cache and lock (StreamUrlCache.kt:18-42). It calls SpotifyStreamProxy.resolveStreamUrl:
   a. The matched videoId comes from Room. An unmatched song is matched on the spot by TrackMatcher.findMatch (SpotifyStreamProxy.kt:119-127, 25 s cap): up to 3 song searches and 1 video search, one after another (TrackMatcher.kt:56-64).
   b. ChainedYouTubeStreamResolver.resolveStream runs with validate = false (YouTubeStreamResolver.kt:255-304). Clients run one at a time, 15 s each (:262-264), VISIONOS first. After them come Piped (15 s) and NewPipe (20 s) (SpotifyStreamProxy.kt:153, :160).
   c. Every player POST needs anonymousVisitorData. That is a blocking NewPipe call made once per process (InnerTubeClient.kt:193-195; PixelPlayPoTokenProvider.kt:58-79).
   d. applyNTransform also runs on pre-signed URLs (YouTubeStreamResolver.kt:86). When the URL carries `n`:
      - iframe_api and base.js (~2.5 MB) are downloaded in every process, with no disk cache (SignatureCipherSolver.kt:100-108, :168-191);
      - a failed download is stored as null, so it is retried for every URL;
      - the first evaluation creates a WebView that first loads https://www.youtube.com/, which can take up to 8 s (JsEvaluator.kt:93-122, :161-163).
      Whether VISIONOS URLs carry `n` is unknown, the same open question as on iOS.
4. The upstream fetch asks for bytes=0-511999 (UPSTREAM_CHUNK_SIZE 512_000, :92, :315-316) and copies the body with channel.writeFully in 64 KB reads (:360-366).
   - VERIFIED IN KTOR 3.5.0 BYTECODE:
     - ByteWriteChannelKt.flushIfNeeded flushes only when the channel is autoFlush or at least 1,048,576 bytes are pending.
     - CIO creates each response's body channel as ByteChannel(autoFlush = false) (ServerPipelineKt startServerConnectionPipeline).
     - CIOApplicationResponse.preparedBodyChannel returns that same channel for a Content-Length response.
     - sendResponseMessage flushes the headers. Nothing flushes the body.
   - Result: ExoPlayer's first read returns only after about 1 MiB has passed through. That is after two full 512,000-byte googlevideo requests and part of a third: three sequential upstream requests plus 1 MiB of transfer before any audio.
   - This is Android's version of iOS root cause #1. It also slows every seek into audio that isn't buffered yet.
5. ExoPlayer waits for bufferForPlaybackMs = 2,500 ms of audio before it starts (buildAdaptiveLoadControl, DualPlayerEngine.kt:995-1027, used at :1158).
   - Media3 1.10.1's own default is 1,000 ms (DefaultLoadControl.DEFAULT_BUFFER_FOR_PLAYBACK_MS; lowered in Media3 1.5.0, per its release notes).
   - The unit-tested loadControlBufferProfileFor (:184-200, LoadControlBufferProfileTest) also says 1,000 ms, but nothing calls it.

NEXT-SONG PREPARATION TODAY
- MusicService.updateNextStreamPrefetch (MusicService.kt:1268-1299):
  - next item only, Spotify only;
  - URL and on-demand match, no bytes;
  - starts 1.5 s in (:1286) and loops every 60 s (:1296).
  Problems:
  - The speculative cache entry lives only 120 s (CloudStreamProxy.kt:85), so a 4-minute song resolves the next one about twice.
  - It reads isPlaying from mediaSession.player (:1273-1274). During Spotify Connect that player is SpotifyConnectSessionPlayer, which reports the remote device's state (SpotifyConnectSessionPlayer.kt:91-97). So it warms local streams while the Echo plays.
  - It never checks Wi-Fi vs cellular or Data Saver.
  - An unmatched next song is searched again every 60 s.
- DualPlayerEngine's 600 ms neighbour pre-resolution (:533-555) runs on every master transition. It calls resolveCloudUri for index+1 and index-1 in timeline order (not shuffle order). Through :1304 that enqueues full-song downloads of BOTH neighbours on any network.
- triggerAdjacentPreResolution (:724-754) filters on http/https, so it does nothing for spotify:// items.
- With crossfade on, TransitionController prepares the next item on playerB 1.5 s into the song (TransitionController.kt:190, :262; DualPlayerEngine.kt:1329-1382). A manual skip discards it (:527-529).
- With gapless (crossfade off), ExoPlayer loads the next playlist item only after the current one is fully loaded, which is about the last 60 s.
- Media3 playlist preloading (ExoPlayer.setPreloadConfiguration: in the API since 1.5.0, off by default, present in 1.10.1) is not used.

recommendedPlan.file: app/src/main/java/com/theveloper/pixelplay/data/diagnostics/StreamStartTimings.kt (new) + DualPlayerEngine.kt:400-405, :511-556, :601-615, :1098-1147 + CloudStreamProxy.kt:224-391 + SpotifyStreamProxy.kt:116-167 + YouTubeStreamResolver.kt:61-91 + PlaybackDispatchStateHolder.kt:898-903 + data/cache/AudioDownloadTransfer.kt:31 + PerformanceMetrics.kt:29-50
recommendedPlan.change:
R12, measure first. Ship this step alone so it records a baseline.
- Add `object StreamStartTimings`: process-wide like PerformanceMetrics, synchronized, holds the last 8 starts keyed by Spotify id, no titles.
  - Use an injectable clock: `var clock: () -> Long = SystemClock::elapsedRealtime`. Under isReturnDefaultValues (app/build.gradle.kts:178), SystemClock returns 0 in JVM tests.
- Marks:
  (a) `requested(id)` in buildResolvedPlaybackMediaItem.
  (b) `begin(id, kind)` in masterPlayerListener.onMediaItemTransition for spotify:// items. The kind comes from the reason: PLAYLIST_CHANGED→TAP, SEEK→SKIP, AUTO→AUTO, REPEAT.
  (c) In the ResolvingDataSource.Resolver: how long resolveCloudUri took, and whether it returned a file.
  (d) Player-side bytes: `DefaultHttpDataSource.Factory().setTransferListener(listener)` (:1143), using androidx.media3.datasource.TransferListener.onTransferStart / onBytesTransferred for dataSpec URIs at 127.0.0.1/spotify/<id>. This gives the true 'player first byte' and the bytes per id.
  (e) STATE_READY (:601) and the first onIsPlayingChanged(true) (:400) end the start.
  (f) Proxy:
    - request arrival (range start; purpose from a new `X-PixelPlay-Purpose: download` header that AudioDownloadTransfer.fetch adds);
    - URL ready (cache hit or ms);
    - upstream headers (ms, status, attempt);
    - first upstream body byte;
    - bytes served, error;
    - requests with no open start are counted as 'background' (preload, warm-up, download).
  (g) SpotifyStreamProxy: match ms (on-demand only), resolve ms, strategy, attempt count.
  (h) PreSignedStreamResolver: `hadN = Uri.parse(best.url).getQueryParameter("n") != null` and the n-transform ms. This splits the 'n sin cambiar' ambiguity, as iOS does.
- Output:
  - one Timber line per start, tag StreamStart, e.g. 'TAP 1840 ms: request→transition 40, dataSpec 12, url 620 (match 0, resolve 610 VISIONOS, n: no), upstream TTFB 140, player first byte 1210, ready 60, playing 30; proxy 1 player + 1 download, 0 retries, preload: no';
  - `lastLine()`;
  - aggregates through PerformanceMetrics: new Timings STREAM_START_TAP/SKIP/AUTO, STREAM_RESOLVE, STREAM_MATCH, STREAM_UPSTREAM_TTFB, STREAM_PLAYER_FIRST_BYTE, STREAM_PROXY_FLUSH_GAP; Counters STREAM_PRELOAD_HITS, STREAM_PROXY_RETRIES, STREAM_EARLY_REBUFFERS (BUFFERING within 10 s of start).
  - DebugPerformanceReport already prints every timing name (DebugPerformanceReport.kt:125-128). No ids go into PerformanceMetrics (privacy rule in docs/performance-report.md).
- All hooks are O(1) and never run on main.

R2 (Android form): deliver bytes as they arrive.
- Extract the copy loop at :357-370 into `internal suspend fun copyUpstream(input: InputStream, channel: io.ktor.utils.io.ByteWriteChannel, limit: Long?, onWritten: (Int) -> Unit): Long`.
- After each `channel.writeFully(buffer, 0, count)`, call `channel.flush()` (a suspend member of ByteWriteChannel in Ktor 3.5.0). Flush still suspends once 1 MiB is unread, so backpressure is unchanged.
- deliveredAnyBytes keeps its meaning. Record the first flush in StreamStartTimings.
- Keep UPSTREAM_CHUNK_SIZE = 512_000. With flushing, the first audio depends on googlevideo's first-byte time, not on the chunk size. iOS's 128 KiB first fetch exists only because AVFoundation waits for a whole response, so it has no Android counterpart.
- Optional, no start gain: grow later chunks 512 KB → 1 MiB → 2 MiB to send fewer requests. Do it only if R12 shows stalls at chunk boundaries mid-song.
- Expected: removes about 1 MiB of transfer and 2 googlevideo round trips from every uncached start and seek. Roughly 0.2-0.5 s on fast Wi-Fi, ~1 s at 10 Mbps, ~3 s at 3 Mbps.

Start streams after 1 s of audio, Media3's default, instead of 2.5 s.
- buildAdaptiveLoadControl uses the tested profile:
  `DefaultLoadControl.Builder()`
  `.setBufferDurationsMsForStreaming(p.minBufferMs, p.maxBufferMs, 1_000, 5_000)`
  `.setBufferDurationsMsForLocalPlayback(p.minBufferMs, p.maxBufferMs, 2_500, 5_000)`
  `.setPrioritizeTimeOverSizeThresholdsForStreaming(true)`
  `.setPrioritizeTimeOverSizeThresholdsForLocalPlayback(true)`
  `.build()`
  (all four setters exist in 1.10.1).
- Media3 decides 'local' from the MediaItem URI scheme (file, content, data, android.resource, rawresource, asset). So spotify:// items, including ones resolved to a cached file, get the streaming values, and local files keep today's 2,500 ms.
- Add `localBufferForPlaybackMs` to LoadControlBufferProfile, update the test, and fix the stale comment at :990-994.
- Watch STREAM_EARLY_REBUFFERS: bufferForPlaybackAfterRebufferMs stays 5,000.

R3 bytes and R7, through Media3's native playlist preloading.
- Add `fun setNextItemPreload(enabled: Boolean)` on the main thread: `playerA.preloadConfiguration = if (enabled) ExoPlayer.PreloadConfiguration(10_000_000L) else ExoPlayer.PreloadConfiguration.DEFAULT`. The class is already @OptIn(UnstableApi::class).
- Keep playerB at DEFAULT.
- Re-apply on every master change: initialize (:781), rebuild (:959), and the crossfade swap (:1489-1500, which also resets the outgoing player).
- MusicService calls it with `depth >= 1` from the same decision point as the URL warm-up. It must switch off explicitly on pause, because ExoPlayer keeps buffering while paused.
- Skip reuse: MediaPeriodQueue.enqueueNextMediaPeriodHolder reuses a matching preloaded holder (removePreloadedMediaPeriodHolder, seen in media3-exoplayer-1.10.1 bytecode). A skip or auto-advance to the preloaded song then starts from memory with no proxy request. That is Android's R7.
- Do NOT port iOS's 'adopt the prepared deck' (taking over crossfade's playerB on a skip): it would need MediaSession player rebinding, and preloading on playerA covers it.
- Data: ProgressiveMediaPeriod checks whether to keep loading only every 1 MiB (ProgressiveMediaSource.DEFAULT_LOADING_CHECK_INTERVAL_BYTES = 1,048,576). Expect roughly 0.5-1 MiB per prepared song, because the proxy's first upstream request is 512,000 bytes. If R12 shows more than the owner's budget, replace DefaultMediaSourceFactory (:1161) with `ProgressiveMediaSource.Factory(resolvingFactory, extractorsFactory).setContinueLoadingCheckIntervalBytes(256 * 1024)`. The app uses no ClippingConfiguration.

R11.
- Add `suspend fun findMatchFanOut(song)`:
  - run queries[0]'s song search alone and keep the early accept (EARLY_ACCEPT_SCORE 0.88);
  - otherwise run the remaining song queries and the queries[0] video search concurrently: `coroutineScope { async { … } }` on the existing Dispatchers.IO calls;
  - fold the results in findMatch's order with the same early-accept, MIN_ACCEPT_SCORE and lastNetworkFailure rules. Count only failures that findMatch would have reached.
  The chosen video is identical, only sooner.
- SpotifyStreamProxy.resolveStreamUrl uses it, for play time and for the warm-ups of the next 1-2 songs from step 5. SpotifyMatchWorker keeps the sequential findMatch.
- Add a 10-min 'no match' memory per Spotify id (`ConcurrentHashMap<String, Long>`), so an unmatchable next song isn't searched 4 times a minute. The DB lookup still runs first, so a later match wins.

recommendedPlan.file: InnerTubeClient.kt:193-195 + PixelPlayPoTokenProvider.kt:58-79 + SignatureCipherSolver.kt:100-108 + CloudStreamProxy.kt:100-114 (optional; decided by R12 numbers)
recommendedPlan.change:
R4, R5a, R6 and R9 on Android.
- R4: nothing to port. Rule for the new hedging flag store (step 9): it is never awaited on the resolve path.
- Only if R12's cold tap shows more than 150 ms for these:
  - call `spotifyStreamProxy.startIfNeeded()` (non-blocking), and warm `poTokenProvider.anonymousVisitorData()` on Dispatchers.IO;
  - both 5 s after MusicService restores a queue whose current item is spotify://, and only with a Spotify account linked (AGENTS: nothing heavy at launch).
- R9, only if R12 shows `n` on VISIONOS URLs:
  - remember a failed base.js download for 60 s; today null is stored and retried for every URL (:104-105);
  - persist the extracted PlayerScript per playerId;
  - warm the JsEvaluator WebView in parallel with the first player POST.
  Leave it out by default.
- R6: skip. OkHttp 5.4.0 has no HTTP/3, and Cronet would be a new network stack.
- R5a: no change; Android is the reference.

Show the timings and write the docs.
- PlaybackDiagnosticsReport gets `lastStreamStart: String?` (StreamStartTimings.lastLine()). run() fills it first, with no network. asPlainText() includes it.
- DiagnosticsCard renders it under the steps: a 'Last stream start' label plus bodySmall text in onSurfaceVariant.
  - Material and glass modes share this composable; only the top bar switches (:100). So both modes get it with no glass-specific work.
  - `succeeded` is unchanged.
- performance-report.md: add the new Timings/Counters rows and a 'Slow to start a streamed song' reading guide. SCHEMA_VERSION stays, because the names flow through the existing map.
- Write the handoff note with the before/after numbers. Tell the iOS integrator to flip the 'Android later' rows in iOS docs/parity.md and list the Android divergences:
  - flush fix instead of a chunk ramp;
  - ExoPlayer preload instead of a head-byte cache;
  - the +2 song gets match + URL only;
  - no player-swap adoption.

recommendedPlan.file: Device measurement protocol (handoff note; Pixel 10 Pro)

tests: ProxyBodyWriterTest (new, JVM, uses ktor-io ByteChannel; Ktor is an `implementation` dependency, so it is available in tests). Feed copyUpstream from a PipedInputStream, write 64 KB, and assert the reader sees `availableForRead >= 65_536` while the writer is still blocked on the pipe. A second case records Ktor 3.5.0's behaviour: plain writeFully leaves under 1 MiB unflushed. That explains the flush; if it fails after a Ktor upgrade, the flush is still harmless.
LoadControlBufferProfileTest (updated): streaming bufferForPlaybackMs = 1_000, local = 2_500, rebuffer = 5_000; both tiers satisfy DefaultLoadControl's ordering asserts.

StreamPrefetchPolicyTest (new): depth = 0 when paused, in a Connect session, under Data Saver or offline; 2 on unmetered Wi-Fi/Ethernet; 1 on metered Wi-Fi, cellular and OTHER. upcomingIndices with a fake next() covers shuffle order, repeat-all wrap, the end of the queue (INDEX_UNSET), and never the current index or a duplicate.
StreamUrlPrefetcherTest (extended): a list prefetch resolves in order; the same list does not restart; a changed list cancels the old job; an empty list cancels.

TrackMatcherFanOutTest (new, mockk InnerTubeClient with `coEvery { searchSongs(any(), any()) } coAnswers { delay(..); list }`): same result as findMatch for early accept on query 0, a later query winning, a video-only match, out-of-order completion, and network failures only from searches findMatch would reach.

HedgedRaceTest (new, kotlinx-coroutines-test virtual time): a slow first strategy loses to a fast second once afterMs passes; a failing first starts the second immediately; the per-strategy timeout applies; the losers are cancelled; with no hedging the chain stays sequential.

StreamRemoteFlagsTest (new): `innertube.hedge.enabled` true/false/missing; afterSeconds and strategyTimeoutSeconds clamped to 0.5-10 and 3-15; malformed JSON, a newer schema or no innertube section all give null (off).

StreamStartTimingsTest (new, injected clock): begin→marks→finish builds the expected line; requests with no open start count as background; preload hit detected; the ring buffer is bounded to 8; nothing id-bearing reaches PerformanceMetrics.

On device, with the owner's permission: protocol S1-S6, plus checks that the Spotify Connect play gate leaves no proxy requests while the Echo plays, that Data Saver means zero background bytes, and that a crossfade with preload on has no audible glitch.
risks: Order matters. Turning on ExoPlayer preload (step 6) before moving the auto-cache (step 4) would trigger full-song SongDownloadWorker downloads of every next song, because preloading calls resolveDataSpec → resolveCloudUri → maybeAutoCache.

Preload byte budget: ProgressiveMediaPeriod reads in 1 MiB steps and loopback socket buffers absorb more, so a prepared-but-skipped song may cost about 0.5-1 MiB, above iOS's 512 KB. R12's background-bytes counter must confirm before cellular preload ships; the fallback is a 256 KiB continue-loading interval through ProgressiveMediaSource.Factory.

A preloaded song keeps an idle proxy→googlevideo connection. If googlevideo closes it, the proxy throws 'ended before its advertised length' (CloudStreamProxy.kt:374), and ExoPlayer reopens at the current offset through DefaultLoadErrorHandlingPolicy, playing the preloaded seconds meanwhile. R12 should count these reconnects. The same already happens today for a long-paused current song.
With crossfade on, playerB (60 s buffer) and playerA's preload both load the next song: duplicate data, bounded by the preload target.

Preloading must be switched off explicitly on pause and during Spotify Connect. ExoPlayer keeps buffering while paused, and MusicService's current gate reads the Connect wrapper (SpotifyConnectSessionPlayer.kt:91-97).
bufferForPlaybackMs 1,000 for streams can cause an early rebuffer on very slow links; the rebuffer threshold stays 5,000 ms and STREAM_EARLY_REBUFFERS watches it.
Flushing every 64 KB adds a suspend call per write (negligible). Flush suspends at 1 MiB unread, so backpressure and the deliveredAnyBytes retry semantics are unchanged.

The flush finding rests on Ktor 3.5.0 bytecode (flushIfNeeded threshold 1,048,576; CIO's per-response ByteChannel(autoFlush = false)). R12's 'player first byte − upstream first byte' gap in build A must confirm it on the device before the savings are claimed.
Raising the speculative URL TTL to 10 min makes stale IP-bound URLs after a Wi-Fi↔cellular switch more likely; the existing refresh-on-403 (CloudStreamProxy.kt:260-279) costs one round trip.

Fan-out matching and depth-2 pre-matching send more YouTube Music searches; hedging (R8) sends more player requests and could raise YouTube's bot scoring for the owner's IP. Hedging stays off until R12 justifies it, and the shared lastFailureReason makes a losing client's diagnostics unreliable.

JVM unit tests cannot exercise CloudStreamProxy or DualPlayerEngine end to end: android.net.Uri, SystemClock, ConnectivityManager and org.json all return defaults under isReturnDefaultValues (app/build.gradle.kts:178). Keep the logic in pure Kotlin helpers; the integration is verified only on the device.
Data Saver's getRestrictBackgroundStatus is a 'use less data' signal, the same role as iOS Low Data Mode; a foreground media service can still use data, so the app must enforce the gate itself.
No PlayerViewModel changes. All new state lives in service-side singletons (AGENTS rule: state holders, not the ViewModel).
ownerDecisions: Full-song 'listening cache': today every Spotify song played, plus the next and previous songs, is downloaded in full on any network, Data Saver included. Suggested: cache only the song actually playing, starting 5 s into it and never under Data Saver. Fully cache the next song only on unmetered Wi-Fi. On cellular, rely on the new short preload.

Preload budget on cellular: Android's native ExoPlayer preload is expected to use about 0.5-1 MiB per upcoming song, not iOS's 512 KB, and it covers only the next song; the second song on Wi-Fi gets match + URL only. Suggested: accept that, measure, and cap at 256 KiB steps only if the measured bytes are over about 1 MiB.

Overlapping-clients flag: should Android read the same `innertube.hedge` switch from the iOS repo's remote/config.json (one switch for both apps)? Suggested: yes; Android reads only the hedge object and keeps its own client table. It stays OFF until the new timings show slow or failing VISIONOS.
Android will not port iOS's 'take over the prepared crossfade deck on skip'; ExoPlayer's preload gives skips the same instant start. Suggested: OK.
R9 (base.js/WebView warm-up) and the optional proxy/visitorData warm-ups ship only if the first-tap timings show they matter. Suggested: leave them out of this batch.
